predecessors.note: Go-Daigo's Kenmu court at Kyoto, ended by Takauji's entry in 1336 (the kenmu-restoration dossier dissolves in February 1336); the Southern Court inherits only the claim and the mountain refuge. The infobox puts the Southern Court's start in 1336.

land.text: the Yoshino holdout and Go-Kameyama's remaining followers, absorbed in the 1392 reunification

successors.note: On 19 November 1392 Go-Kameyama renounced the Imperial Treasures to the Northern Court (Nanboku-chō page); the Southern Court page's infobox gives 11 August 1392.

capitals.name: Yoshino
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Yoshino, Yoshino Province. The Nanboku-chō page: Go-Daigo set up the court 'in the mountains of Yoshino'. Other seats are not on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Go-Daigo
rulers.note: Reigned 1318-1339 in all (Nanboku-chō page); the infobox gives his Southern Court reign as 1336-1339.

rulers.name: Go-Kameyama
rulers.note: Abdicated; renounced the Imperial Treasures on 19 November 1392.

correction.text: the mountains of Yoshino, where Go-Daigo 'set up the Southern Court' in January 1337

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its Kenmu Restoration row, 1333-1343, draws the whole realm of Go-Daigo). The pages give a refuge, not a territory: the Southern Court's land is the Yoshino mountains (a 30 km circle, about 2,800 km2 by the gazetteer, as in the ashikaga-shogunate dossier). Kyushu resistance and the Kyoto episodes of 1351 and 1362 are ledger events (contest, occupation). No page gives an area.

ledger.note: 1337: two courts, one realm. The Southern Court at Yoshino against Takauji's Northern Court at Kyoto; mirrors the ashikaga-shogunate contest of the same year.

region.text: Kyushu, where resistance to the Ashikaga lasted to 1385

ledger.note: 1337: Kyushu. The ashikaga-shogunate dossier opens its Kyushu contest in 1336, when Takauji retreated there; the Nanboku-chō page names Southern resistance in Kyushu only when Imagawa Sadayo is sent against it in 1370, so the Southern side of the zone is the sister dossier's reading (confidence 1).

1337: Go-Daigo sets up the Southern Court at Yoshino. 'In January 1337, Go-Daigo escaped the capital and set up the Southern Court in the mountains of Yoshino'; the regalia he gave the Ashikaga were counterfeit. The infobox starts the court in 1336 and gives Yoshino as capital.

1351: Kyoto falls to the Southern side. Ashikaga Tadayoshi joined the Southern Court in 1350 and was appointed general of its army; 'In 1351, Tadayoshi defeated Takauji, occupied Kyoto, and entered Kamakura'; 'Go-Murakami briefly ruled all of Japan between 1351 and 1352'.

1352: Takauji recovers the capital. The page says 'In 1352, Takauji defeated Tadayoshi at Sattayama'; it does not say when Kyoto was given back, but the Southern offensives of 1353 and 1354 'against Kyoto' show it was Ashikaga again.
1362: the last Southern offensive. It 'forced the Ashikaga to withdraw from the capital'.
1362: Kyoto lost again. 'The Southern forces eventually retreated after a large counterattack.'

1385: the last Southern resistance in Kyushu ends. Imagawa Sadayo was appointed in 1370 to destroy it; 'resistance collapsed with the defeat of the Kikuchi clan in 1381'; 'The death of Shimazu Ujihisa in 1385 ended the last Kyūshū domain's resistance.'

1392: the two courts become one. 'On November 19, 1392, Go-Kameyama renounced the Imperial Treasures to the Northern Court', in exchange for an agreement to alternate succession (broken in 1412). The Southern Court infobox gives 11 August 1392 for the reunification.

region.text: Yoshino and the last Southern followers

ledger.note: 1392: the Southern Court ends. Go-Kameyama abdicates; the page's 'ending his lineage's claim'. In 1911 an imperial decree dated 3 March made the Southern Court emperors the legitimate rulers of the period.

wars.name: Nanboku-chō wars
wars.outcome: The Ashikaga's Northern Court prevailed: the Southern resistance in the central provinces ended with Kusunoki Masanori's submission in 1369, in Kyushu in 1381-1385, and Go-Kameyama surrendered the regalia in 1392.
wars.note: At Minatogawa in 1336 Takauji beat Nitta Yoshisada and killed Kusunoki Masashige.

wars.name: Kannō disturbance
wars.outcome: Tadayoshi, joined to the Southern Court, occupied Kyoto in 1351; Takauji defeated him at Sattayama in 1352.
wars.note: The page also records Southern offensives against Kyoto in 1353 and 1354 (Yamana Tokiuji defected in 1353) and the last in 1362.

wars.name: Imagawa Sadayo's Kyushu campaign
wars.outcome: Twelve years of campaign: the Kikuchi were defeated in 1381; Shimazu Ujihisa's death in 1385 ended the last domain's resistance.

certainty.note: Yoshino is a refuge, not a surveyed territory; the Kyushu and Kyoto episodes are approximate.

sources.title: Southern Court
sources.note: Infobox: capital Yoshino, reigns Go-Daigo 1336-1339, Go-Murakami 1339-1368, Chokei 1368-1383, Go-Kameyama 1383-1392, reunification 11 Aug 1392; claims 1336-1392; preceded by the Kenmu Restoration. Thin on land.

sources.title: Nanboku-chō period
sources.note: Jan 1337 Yoshino court; 1351-1352 Tadayoshi occupies Kyoto; 1353, 1354, 1362 offensives; 1369 Kusunoki Masanori submits; 1370-1385 Kyushu campaign, Kikuchi 1381, Shimazu Ujihisa 1385; 19 Nov 1392 Go-Kameyama renounces the regalia.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from two pages (Southern Court, Nanboku-chō period). Cliopatria has no row for the Southern Court (the Kenmu Restoration row runs 1333-1343 over Go-Daigo's whole realm). The pages give the court's refuge (Yoshino), its emperors, the Kyushu resistance and the Kyoto episodes of 1351-1352 and 1362, but no territory list: nothing on Kii, Kanto or Tohoku strongholds (the Southern Court page says so; the Nanboku-chō page names Kitabatake Akiie and Nitta Yoshisada only in 1335-1336). Hitachi (a long siege during which Kitabatake Chikafusa wrote the Jinnō Shōtōki) is on the Nanboku-chō page without years of its own, so it is not drawn. Start 1337 (Jan) from the body; infobox 1336. End: body 19 November 1392, infobox 11 August 1392; November follows the ashikaga-shogunate dossier. Ashikaga counterpart events: contest_start 1336 (Kyushu), 1337 (Yoshino), contest_end 1385, 1392, mirrored here; the 1336/1337 Kyushu year differs by one. The 1351 and 1362 occupations are not in the ashikaga-shogunate dossier. 1369 (Kusunoki Masanori submits, 'ending the Southern threat to the central provinces') moved no named land. Prince Kaneyoshi's Kyushu court is not on either page. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
